_about: Hand-maintained rules for /fedramp-lookup/. Each listing is assigned one case by scripts/fedramp/build_lookup.py; each case answers every row. Edit the wording here and push to rebuild. Every case must answer every row, or the build fails. States: lev = package can be leveraged, dec = agency risk decision, no = not recognized, wait = not yet available. {status} in a note is replaced with the listing's marketplace status; {host} with the hosting listing's name. The 'hosted' case is for third-party products a platform lists as services inside its own authorization (see hosted-services.json). In banners, **text** is shown bold and a blank line starts a new paragraph.

hosted_banner:
**Listed inside another provider’s authorization.** {hostProvider} lists {service} as a service within {host} ({hostId}). A FedRAMP certification covers only the information resources the provider identified and had assessed as its offering; anything outside that set is not FedRAMP Certified (CR26 MAS-CSO-IIR, MAS-CSO-SUP). The marketplace’s service list is supplied by the provider, and the marketplace rules set no check of it against the assessed scope. If {service} was added after assessment, adding a critical third-party service is a transformative significant change, where third-party assessment is recommended, not required (SCN-TRF-TPR), and a report is required only if one applies (SCN-TRF-NAV). For DoD contractors, DFARS 7012 applies to the cloud service you actually use, which here is {service}.

**Treat {service} as not authorized unless** it has its own FedRAMP listing; it meets FedRAMP Moderate equivalency under the DoD CIO memo of 21 Dec 2023 (annual 3PAO assessment, all controls met, full body of evidence); or the {host} package shows it inside the assessed scope or covered by an assessed significant change. If a vendor gave you {hostId} as this product’s FedRAMP ID, that is the host’s ID, not the product’s.
host_banner: Given this ID for a different product? {hostId} is the ID of {host} itself. The products below are listed as services inside it but have no FedRAMP listing of their own, and the ticks on this card do not extend to them. A vendor quoting this ID for one of them is quoting the host’s authorization, not its own.
pilot_banner: Pilot certification, relabeled {class}. This listing was certified in the FedRAMP 20x pilot on {date}, before certification classes existed; the marketplace later labeled it {class}. FedRAMP’s presumption of adequacy for {class} describes packages built to the CR26 requirements for that class, which this listing was not. CR26’s 20x significant change rules (SCN-*) take effect for ongoing certification on 1 Jan 2027, so until then nothing requires this listing to notify anyone of changes.
class_a_banner: No significant change rules. CR26’s 20x significant change rules cover Classes B, C and D; Class A is not covered, so a Class A listing has no rule requiring it to notify anyone when the service changes.
